questions.q: According to this lesson, how can an AI system's accuracy quietly decline even though the model's weights never changed after launch?
options: The data flowing into the model shifts over time — customer language, product mix, topics — so inputs stop resembling what the model was built or evaluated on
The model automatically retrains itself every night without anyone noticing
Accuracy can never decline unless the model's weights are changed
The server hosting the model silently downgrades its hardware
questions.explain: Even an unchanged model can perform worse once the real-world input distribution no longer matches what it was built or validated against.

questions.q: What is the difference between data drift and concept drift, as defined in this lesson?
options: Data drift is a change in the input distribution; concept drift is a change in what counts as the correct output for a given input
Data drift and concept drift are two names for exactly the same thing
Data drift only applies to images, while concept drift only applies to text
Concept drift means the input distribution changed; data drift means the model's code changed
questions.explain: Data drift is about the inputs themselves shifting; concept drift is about the relationship between input and correct output shifting.

questions.q: What does a drift report's reference vs. current distribution comparison actually show, per the screenshot in this lesson?
options: A random sample of unrelated columns with no comparison at all
Each column's distribution at baseline compared against a current window, with a stat test and drift score flagging whether it shifted
Only whether the model's accuracy number increased or decreased
A list of every individual record in the dataset
questions.explain: The report compares a reference (baseline) distribution against a current window, column by column, using a stat test suited to that column's type.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say a drift report is more useful as an automated pass/fail test suite than as a report someone has to remember to check?
options: Test suites are always less accurate than manual review
A report nobody checks gets ignored, while a pass/fail gate with a threshold lets a pipeline act automatically — block a deploy, open a ticket, trigger retraining
Pass/fail gates cannot name which specific column drifted
Automated gates eliminate the need to ever look at distributions
questions.explain: Turning the same checks into a threshold-based test suite is what lets drift detection trigger an automatic action instead of depending on someone remembering to look.

questions.q: How does this lesson say drift detection applies to an LLM app that doesn't have a classic tabular dataset?
options: Drift detection is impossible for any AI system that isn't a traditional ML model
LLM apps never experience any form of drift
Only the final production accuracy number can be tracked, nothing else
The same reference-vs-current comparison can track prompt topics, retrieved documents, or the model's own output tone and length
questions.explain: The same reference-window-vs-current-window approach extends to prompt distributions, RAG retrieval, and output characteristics in an LLM system.
